Chapter 1 introduces the Manager Over/Underperformance (MOU) Index as a framework to quantify how effectively managers elevate player performance beyond expectations. It establishes the foundational premise that while player performance statistics are abundant, managerial impact remains underanalyzed. The core innovation lies in applying predictive modeling to isolate manager-specific contributions to performance variation. The index is constructed using a delta between actual and predicted player performance, normalized by the latter and adjusted by a dampening factor to penalize managers with limited seasonal data. This approach allows for granular comparison across managers and positions, addressing prior literature's reliance on aggregate team-level analysis. The inclusion of a dampening factor κ_κ ensures robustness against spurious performance claims from short-term managers. The framework supports both squad-level and position-group-level evaluations, enabling nuanced understanding of managerial strengths and weaknesses. It builds upon earlier work in sports analytics, particularly in baseball, where managerial efficiency was assessed via survival and win probability models. However, unlike those studies, this work focuses on soccer's unique structure—where one manager governs a complex, multi-role squad—and applies stochastic frontier methods to estimate optimal performance boundaries. The index thus bridges empirical data with theoretical modeling, offering a scalable method for evaluating managerial excellence.
